updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Tip family (E046 code: bs 1536, 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 ep, compiled Muon on 9 convs + head): ~4.95 s, but its pooled accuracy over 5 same-math runs (E046, E048, E052, E053, E056) is only 0.7533, which is at the gate. Two math-equivalent speedups are measured but not banked: static per-resolution graphs (-2.0%, E053) and a global max via flatten(2).max(dim=2).values instead of AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) (another -2.9%, E056), together 4.718 s. Banking them needs about +0.1-0.2 pp of accuracy at zero time cost. Cost structure: the 32 px tail is ~71% of time and energy-bound at the 400 W cap. 16 px is low-occupancy (98% GPU-busy, E052), not launch-bound, so CUDA graphs and launch levers are closed. Remaining time levers, ranked: (a) math-neutral kernel efficiency (fused BN/GELU elementwise, ~30% of GPU time, E052) and FLOP removal at no accuracy cost (whitening-bias freeze removes the group-1 conv1 dgrad); (b) equal-time schedule reshuffles (E047); (c) width cuts, only after a per-layer profile; (d) fractional trims, only once accuracy slack exists.
updates.reason: Re-baselined to the pooled 0.7533 (review). E052 refutes the launch-bound reading of 16 px. E053/E056 confirm the math-neutral time levers. Lever ranking updated.

updates.statement: Phase-dependent bottleneck. 32 px (cap 94-100% of the time) and 24 px (cap 84%) are energy-bound, so time tracks fwd/bwd energy and memory traffic. 16 px is not at the cap (282 W) but is 98% GPU-busy (E052), so it is bound by low-occupancy small kernels and per-step GPU work (Muon NS/momentum, SGD foreach, lookahead), not by idle gaps or launches. E038's ~2 ms per removed step was per-step GPU work. Levers: less per-step GPU work, larger fused kernels, or fewer FLOPs/bytes. FLOP and byte levers transfer best to the 300 W PCIe judge.
updates.reason: E052 (98/99/100% busy per phase) refutes the 'launch-bound 16 px' part. The energy-bound part stands (E004, E010, E045).
E052: busy/wall was 98% at 16 px, so wall time did not exceed GPU-busy time by >=30%.
Its premise (idle gaps at 16 px) is refuted by E052 (98% busy). Fable also reports minimal gains from CUDA graphs and optimizer fusion under fair retiming (search).
The gate (H2.4.2) failed: E052 shows no idle gaps at 16 px.
The gate (H2.4.2) failed (E052). There are no idle gaps for the overlap to fill.

updates.statement: Compile and graph configuration is a FLOP-neutral time lever. Static per-resolution graphs (automatic_dynamic_shapes=False, cache_size_limit 64) saved 2.0% (E053). Replacing AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1), whose atomic backward cost ~0.8 ms/step (E052), with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values saved another 2.9% (E056). Under torch 2.4 Inductor fp16, amax produces NaNs in backward (E055), so use max(dim).values. Both changes are math-equivalent but not bit-equivalent (fp16 ties, different kernel picks). Static shapes + max pool (E056 code, 4.718 s) is the base code for all later experiments.
updates.reason: E053+ and E056+ confirmed both predicted time gains.
E053: 4.858 s (-2.0%) with eager eval (no eval recompiles). Its accuracy (0.7524) is inside the tip family's spread (pooled 0.7533).
E056: -0.140 s (-2.9%) vs E053 using max(dim).values. The accuracy (0.7525) is in the family spread. E055 showed the amax variant crashes under Inductor fp16.

updates.statement: Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are the finest schedule lever. E047 (2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32, 7.5 ep) matched E046's time (4.963 vs 4.955 s) and scored 0.7558 on one run, +0.25 pp over the pooled tip 0.7533. Fewer total steps with more 24 px may be a better equal-time schedule than the 3@16 swap. Its '0.03 pp per 1%' slope was measured against single-trajectory E044, so it is unreliable. E054 (3@16 + 0.75@24, static) scored -0.14 pp vs pooled for -2.6%. With ~0 margin, accuracy-costing trims are unbankable; the equal-time reshuffle (E047 schedule on the E056 base) is the immediate candidate.
updates.reason: Re-baselined to the pooled 0.7533 (review). E047 was discarded only against a lucky E046 draw.
Arm A (0.5@24) trims further than E054 (0.75@24), which already fell below the gate at ~0 margin. Superseded by the equal-time E047-schedule test on the E056 base.

updates.statement: 16 px epochs are cheap (0.30x of a 32 px epoch at bs 1536, E045). Each early 24->16 swap costs roughly 0.2-0.35 pp, but these are single-run point estimates against references that were often lucky draws (±0.15 pp). The third swap (E046) cost more than the head-on-Muon gain bought: the tip family pools to 0.7533. No further whole-epoch swap is affordable. Giving part of the 24 px bridge back while cutting total epochs (E047) may beat the 3@16 swap at equal time.
updates.reason: Re-baselined: E046's 'margin ~0.2 pp' was a lucky draw. The pooled family mean is 0.7533 (E048, E052, E053, E056).
E043 is confounded by the warmup step count. With ~0 accuracy margin, batch levers that risk accuracy are unattractive.
Low priority. It risks early-training accuracy when there is no margin, and its gate (H8.1.1) is itself low priority.

updates.statement: Muon flattened the epoch slope, so a group-2 width cut might trade like a schedule trim. Against the pooled 0.7533, E050 (384->352) is -0.07 pp for -2.6% (~0.03 pp per 1%), the same rate as trims, not 0.085. Its time saving was half the FLOP estimate, possibly from tile misalignment (352 is not a multiple of 64/128) or because group-2 FLOPs at 16 px barely become time. A FLOP lever like this transfers best to the 300 W judge, but needs a per-layer profile (H2.13.2) before any scored run.
updates.reason: Re-baselined per the review. The E050 conclusion depended on the inflated 0.7548 reference.
Stays refuted on its time prediction (-2.6% < 3.5%). The accuracy side is noise against the pooled 0.7533.
Now the gate for any width run. It is cheap and untimed, and it would explain E050's time shortfall.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and the loop has selected for luck. Five runs of the tip math (E046 0.7553, E048 0.7543, E052 0.7518, E053 0.7524, E056 0.7525) pool to 0.7533 (per-run sd ~0.15 pp, SE ~0.07). The local margin is ~0. The official 75% margin is ~0.35-0.45 pp (seeds 3-10 mean 0.7542, E048). Single-run verdicts with |Δ| < ~0.3 pp are inconclusive. Earlier 'closures' (E030, E034, E037, E049, E051) only mean 'no effect larger than ~0.3 pp on that base'. Promotion rule: compare against the pooled family mean, never a single draw. A new tip needs a pooled mean >=0.7540 over >=3 non-bit-identical runs, or >=2 runs each >=0.7545. Do not rerun E056 unchanged hoping it clears. Time noise ~0.3%. Provenance: E028/E048/E052 descriptions named older code than their timings imply, so log a hash of the submission source in every row.
updates.reason: The review's re-baselining: E046 was the high draw of a 0.7533 distribution (E052, E053, E056 added). The old promotion rule admitted it.

updates.statement: Run-to-run noise (~0.15 pp sd on a 3-seed mean), not cross-seed std, is the decision-relevant noise floor. Picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck: E026 was ~0.1 pp lucky, and E046 ~0.2 pp lucky (pooled family 0.7533). Every comparison should use pooled multi-run baselines.
updates.reason: E046 adds a second, larger instance of selection for luck (E052, E053, E056 pooled).
No new direct test. A related run-level-offset reading is added as a new child of H4.

updates.statement: Zero-time-cost accuracy levers must supply the ~+0.1-0.2 pp needed to bank E056's -4.8% (4.718 s). Against the pooled 0.7533, head Muon lr 0.5x (E049, 0.7558) reads +0.25 pp, the best single zero-cost signal. LS 0.2 (E037) and halved warmup (E051, -0.05 pp re-baselined) are nulls within noise. Candidates tied to the ~256-step regime: replicating head lr 0.5x on the E056 base (H7.3), Muon LR floor 0.05 plus a Fable-style floor-held tail and short final EMA (H6.5), whitening-bias freeze after 20% of steps (also a FLOP lever), and small decoupled wd on the Muon head. Budget 2 runs per arm. Low-prior: NorMuon row normalization (LLM-only evidence) and HTMuon (+0.29 pp on CIFAR-100, but only with long training and SVD).
updates.reason: Re-baselined. E049 moves from noise to the best signal. Search adds Fable/hiverge candidates.

updates.statement: The LR warmup was rescaled from ~408 SGD steps to ~256 steps (bs 1536). Halving it (E051, 0.7528) is -0.05 pp against the pooled 0.7533, which is noise, so neither direction is established. The post-mortem mechanism ('warmup protects the 64x-LR SGD biases') has no supporting effect.
updates.reason: Re-baselined: E051's -0.2 pp was measured against the lucky E046 draw.
Against the pooled 0.7533, E051 is -0.05 pp: within noise in both directions. A single run cannot close it.

updates.statement: On the E056 base (static shapes + max pool), double the LR warmup length for both the SGD and Muon groups (same peak and decay end point), and change nothing else. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 (+0.15 pp over the pooled 0.7533) at equal time (±0.5%). A result within ±0.15 pp closes warmup length in both directions.
updates.reason: Rebased to the E056 base and the pooled baseline. Priority lowered because E051 is a null, not a signal.

updates.statement: The LR floor (0.07x) and lookahead-EMA ramp were tuned under SGD (E015). Both public bs-1536 Muon records (Fable e1, hiverge) instead decay to a 0.05 floor and hold it for a short tail. Fable adds a light final EMA over the last ~8 steps (every 4 steps, decay 0.7). Muon's normalized updates may suit the lower floor and the short final average better. These are zero-time levers.
updates.reason: Search: Fable e1's schedule gives direct external support.

updates.statement: On the E056 base, change the Muon-group LR floor from 0.07x to 0.05x and nothing else. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 (+0.15 pp over the pooled 0.7533) at equal time (±0.5%). A result within ±0.15 pp closes it.
updates.reason: Rebased to the E056 base and the pooled baseline. The two-run requirement follows the new H4 rule.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~8 epochs, and Muon was the lever. On the 9 group convs it gave +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020) and large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Putting the head on Muon was reported as +0.32 pp (E044), but that is one trajectory against one (E045 was a bit-identical replay). The indirect estimate from the pooled family vs E029/E040 is about +0.1-0.2 pp, so plan with ~+0.15. The head's update scale looks like a live knob (E049, H7.3). Muon lr, momentum, NS count and LS nulls were single runs on older bases: they rule out effects larger than ~0.3 pp, not +0.15 pp. Cheaper orthogonalizers are closed: E031, E033, and MUD gave no wall-clock gain on airbench (search).
updates.reason: Head-gain size revised down (review). Closures restated as bounded. MUD evidence added.

MUD (search) found no wall-clock gain from cheaper orthogonalization on airbench Muon, consistent with E031 and E033. An fp16 momentum buffer (hiverge) is a possible tiny saving and is not worth its own scored run.
Low prior after MUD (no CNN wall-clock gain, -0.7 pp) and E033 (orthogonalization quality is saturated at 3 steps, and 2 steps cost 1.8 pp). The ~1.5% ceiling is not worth an offline study now.

updates.statement: On the E056 base (bs 1536, ~256 steps, head on Muon), change only the conv-filter Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.28 (0-d tensor, nothing recompiles). Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 (+0.15 pp over the pooled 0.7533) at equal time. A result within ±0.15 pp means the bs-1024 lr optimum transfers.
updates.reason: Rebased. Ranked below the head lr, floor/EMA and whitening-bias candidates.

updates.statement: The head's update scale is a live accuracy knob. Head-on-Muon helped (+~0.15 pp, H7), and halving the head's Muon lr then read +0.25 pp against the pooled 0.7533 (E049, single run). Both point to the step size or update scale on the 100-way head, not only orthogonalization. Public bs-1536 records keep the head on SGD (lr ~0.54, logits divided by the feature dim, std-normalized init). The Muon head has no wd or renorm. Cheap head levers (lr, wd, logit scale) could supply the margin needed to bank E056.
updates.reason: E049 re-read against the pooled baseline (review). Search: Fable/hiverge head handling and Muon wd evidence.
A mechanism probe that cannot buy time. Ranked below the head-lr replicate.

updates.statement: Early-training fragility: in the ~256-step regime, the quantity and quality of early updates might bound final accuracy. Re-baselined, its pillars weaken. E051 (halved warmup) is noise (-0.05 pp). E043 (-0.49 pp) is confounded by the warmup step count. The 16 px swap costs are single runs against lucky references. Only E032 (no 24 px bridge, -0.68 pp) is large. Treat as a weak prior: avoid levers that coarsen early training, but do not spend runs testing it directly unless a lever doubles as a time saving (e.g. whitening-bias freeze).
updates.reason: Review: most of H8's support was measured against the inflated 0.7548 baseline.

The bias-LR channel gets indirect support from Fable/hiverge (whitening bias trained only for the first 20% of steps), but no effect has been observed here. Tested via the whitening-bias freeze child of H2.
Low priority. It needs 2 runs per arm to resolve +0.15 pp, and its motivating effects are mostly noise after re-baselining.
The motivating effect (E051 -0.2 pp) is -0.05 pp against the pooled 0.7533, so there is nothing to localize.

new.statement: On the E056 base (static shapes + max(dim).values pool), run E047's schedule 2@16 + 1.5@24 + 4@32 px (7.5 ep, step-indexed switches, LR/EMA/lookahead/renorm rescaled to the step count). Run it twice, as one factor of a 2x2 with head lr 0.5x so the arms share baselines. Prediction: time <=4.74 s (equal to E056 within 0.5%) and a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7540, i.e. >=+0.07 pp over the pooled 0.7533. If both runs land <=0.7530, E047's 0.7558 was a lucky draw.

On the E056 base, set the head's Muon lr to 0.5x the filter lr (0.12 peak, a separate 0-d tensor) and change nothing else; run it twice. Prediction: time within ±0.5% of 4.718 s and a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7540 (together with E049's 0.7558, a 3-run pool >=0.7545). If it passes the H4 rule, it becomes the new tip at ~4.72 s. If the two runs average <=0.7530, E049 was noise and head lr is closed.

On the E056 base, add decoupled weight decay to the Muon head weight only (wd*lr ≈ 1.6e-3 per step scale, hiverge's bs-1536 setting), so its norm is bounded like the renormed filters. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 at equal time. Low prior: the only evidence is an unverified search snippet (+0.34 pp on CIFAR-10 with long training).

On the E056 base, use Fable's tail at equal total steps: the LR decay ends ~4% of steps early and holds at a 0.05 floor for the rest. A light final EMA (every 4 steps, ema = 0.7*ema + 0.3*net over the last ~8 steps, foreach_lerp) replaces the end of the lookahead-EMA ramp, and evaluation uses the EMA weights. Prediction: a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7548 at equal time (±0.5%).

Freezing the whitening bias after ~20% of steps (Fable e1, hiverge; airbench reports no accuracy loss) leaves the stem without trainable parameters for the remaining steps. Autograd can then skip group-1 conv1's input gradient (dgrad) at the highest resolution in every 24/32 px step. Estimated saving: ~1-3% of fwd+bwd FLOPs. It is a FLOP lever, so it should transfer to the power-capped PCIe judge. It also removes the 64x-LR bias channel of H8.1 for most of the run. First verify that the tip trains this bias for the whole run.

On the E056 base, set the whitening bias requires_grad=False after 20% of steps (inside the 16 px phase), with separate static compiled graphs keyed by bias-grad, all warmed up in build on synthetic data. Change nothing else, and run twice. Prediction: time <=4.67 s (>=1% below 4.718 s) and a two-run pooled accuracy >=0.7525 (within noise of 0.7533). If the time drop is <0.3%, the dgrad is not actually being skipped (check the compiled backward graph).

The fused BN/GELU/elementwise Triton kernels take ~30% of GPU time in every phase (E052). They are memory-traffic and energy bound, and nothing has targeted them yet. Fewer passes over each fp16 activation (BN stats + apply + GELU fused in forward; recompute-friendly fused backward) would cut bytes moved at identical math. That saving is energy-proportional, so it should help both the capped 24/32 px phases and the 300 W PCIe judge. Try Inductor-level options first (fusion/tuning flags, warmed up in build), then a hand-written Triton kernel.

Untimed profiler breakdown on the E056 base at 32 px, bs 1536. Per conv layer per step, the BN/GELU forward and backward make >=4 full read/write passes over the fp16 activation, and the elementwise/reduction kernels take >=25% of GPU time. If they take <15% or already run at <=2 passes, the lever is dead and N_elem is refuted.

Gated on N_elem_1. On the E056 base, a fused BN-apply+GELU forward/backward (compile flags, or a custom Triton kernel for the 24/32 px shapes, warmed up in build) cuts time by >=2% (<=4.62 s). Accuracy stays within noise: math-equivalent up to fp16 rounding, two-run pooled >=0.7525. Write down the bytes-moved prediction before scoring.

Part of the run-to-run variance is a per-run offset shared by all 3 trials. It would come from cuDNN algorithm picks (cudnn.benchmark) cached once per process in build and reused across trials. Some pick sets (e.g. fp16 Winograd/FFT paths) may cost accuracy systematically. Weak current support: the within-run per-seed sd over the 5 family runs averages ~0.18 pp, which implies a 3-seed-mean sd of ~0.11, against the observed ~0.15. Some runs are tight (E052 0.7514-0.7521) and others wide (E046 0.7523-0.7572), and no seed effect is visible. If confirmed, restricting the pick set in build (without deterministic=True, which costs 9.8%) would be an accuracy lever.

Untimed diagnostic over the next >=4 scored runs: log the cuDNN conv kernel names per (layer, shape) from profiler kernel names in build/first steps. Prediction: runs sharing the same algorithm set have run means within 0.1 pp, and at least one set tracks a lower mean by >=0.2 pp. If the algorithm sets are identical across runs while the means still differ by >=0.2 pp, the offset is not caused by algorithm picks and N_h4_5 is refuted.

Provenance check, untimed. Diffing commits e6c8e93 (E048) and 4fd9ea5 (E052) against 2fda094 (E046) shows only instrumentation/logging changes. 5a77f89 (E053) and 6262ecd (E056) differ only by the static-shape config and the pool. On one fixed batch, the gradients of flatten(2).max(dim=2).values and AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) match except at fp16 ties. If any of these fails, the pooled 0.7533 family baseline must be recomputed without the affected runs.

structured_output.summary:
Re-baselined the tree on the pooled tip-family mean of 0.7533. That is five runs of the same math (E046, E048, E052, E053, E056) with sd ~0.15 pp, which replaces the lucky single-draw 0.7548. The local margin is about 0. The math-neutral speedups are confirmed (H2.14, H2.14.1, H2.14.2 supported: static shapes -2.0%, max(dim).values pool another -2.9%, 4.718 s), and the E056 code is now the base. They can only be banked with ~+0.1-0.2 pp of zero-time accuracy.

Changes after re-baselining:
- E051 becomes noise: H6.4.1 and H6.4 are inconclusive, H8.1.2 is retired, and H8 drops to 0.2.
- E049 (head Muon lr 0.5x) is now the best zero-cost signal at +0.25 pp. H7.3 is reframed around head update scale, and a two-run replicate on the E056 base is added.
- E047's schedule may beat the 3@16 swap at equal time; an equal-time test on the E056 base is added under H2.10.
- E050's width cut now trades like a schedule trim, so H2.13 is inconclusive and gated on the per-layer profile.
- The head-on-Muon gain is revised down to ~+0.15 pp.

E052 (98% busy at 16 px) refutes the launch-bound reading. H2.4.2 is refuted, H2.12 and its children are retired, H2.4 is rewritten as occupancy-bound, and the MUD finding led to retiring H7.2.4. H4 gets a stricter promotion rule: pooled >=0.7540 over >=3 non-bit-identical runs, or >=2 runs each >=0.7545, plus provenance logging.

New directions:
- Whitening-bias freeze after 20% of steps (Fable/hiverge/airbench): a FLOP lever that drops group-1 conv1's dgrad.
- Fused BN/GELU elementwise kernels (~30% of GPU time), profile first.
- Fable floor-held tail + short final EMA.
- Decoupled wd on the Muon head.
- A run-level cuDNN-pick offset under H4, with weak current support.
- A provenance/pool-gradient check.

Recommended next step: a 2x2 of head lr 0.5x × the E047 schedule on the E056 base, two runs per arm, each judged against the pooled 0.7533.
